长剑
The entity 长剑 is described as a sharp, offensive, and well-balanced weapon renowned for its cutting edge and agile performance in combat. Multiple accounts note its physical attributes as a finely crafted, three-foot-long sword with a keen, pointed tip, emphasizing its readiness for swift attacks in battle.

The 长剑 appears in diverse martial contexts. It is notably used by warriors such as the 青衣剑士 (Blue-clothed swordsmen), who employed it in duels and battle, even to the point of having to wipe off blood after combat. In another account, the 锦衫剑士 (Brocade-clothed swordsman) is recorded using a similar sword during a sword-testing session, where the weapon unexpectedly fractured, suggesting either a moment of vulnerability or the exceptional rigors of combat training. Additionally, the 长剑 is recognized as an instrument of state power and duty, with mentions of its use by卫士 (guards) not only in battle alongside 吴国剑士 (Wu swordsmen) but also in missions to execute orders and to protect figures such as 范蠡.

Furthermore, the 武器 is also referenced as part of the armaments of the 越军 (soldiers of Yue) during warfare, highlighting its role across different military factions and historical narratives. The inclusion of an English description—"Long swords employed by the Wu swordsmen during battle"—underscores its broader recognition and usage in various battle scenarios.

Overall, the collected descriptions of 长剑 reveal a multifaceted weapon esteemed for its precision and lethal efficiency, integral to the martial traditions and historical narratives of several distinguished warrior groups.

绝世美女(夷光)，曾与少伯情深，后被送入吴宫<SEP>A renowned beauty whom范蠡eagerly anticipates reuniting with.<SEP>传说中范蠡真正细看过的绝世美女<SEP>吴国美女，居住于馆娃宫，与范蠡互诉相思<SEP>范蠡宠爱的女子，深受其关爱，同时引发阿青由敌对转为崇敬的情感

甲士

范蠡
范蠡, the historical figure associated with the state of Yue, is portrayed as an influential adviser and official who played a multifaceted role during a turbulent period in Chinese history. He is traditionally known to have served under King Goujian, where he not only received and showcased gifts but also provided critical counsel in statecraft, military strategy, and diplomacy. Accounts emphasize his involvement in matters ranging from the forging of swords for combat to commanding guards and orchestrating military operations, including leading troops against enemy strongholds. In addition to his strategic acumen, this version of 范蠡 is noted for his personal pursuits, such as his famed quest for the beauty Xi Shi and his support for figures like 阿青 through negotiation and direct command. Celebrated for his unconventional yet kind-hearted approach, he remains remembered as someone who balanced tactical brilliance with personal charm, leaving a lasting impact on Yue’s successes in both internal administration and external conflicts.

A distinct portrayal of 范蠡 emerges from records concerning the Chu region. This version of 范蠡 is described as a native of the Wan area in Chu, recognized for his unorthodox behavior and unconventional outlook. Known locally by the nickname “范疯子,” he served as a local official and was also depicted as a shepherd who recounted legendary Chu stories. His actions, which noticeably deviated from societal norms, earned him a reputation for being an individual with singular insights and a distinctive character. While sharing the same name, these contrasting accounts highlight separate interpretations of 范蠡’s legacy across different cultural and regional contexts.
